blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An HR directory runs `SELECT name, title FROM employee ORDER BY ` + sort, after checking that sort matches `[a-z_]+`. The employee table also has a salary column, which the directory never shows. A user sends sort=salary. What does the user get?

options.text: The directory ordered by salary, since the pattern checks only the characters and salary is a column of the employee table
options.says: a shape check accepts any identifier, and ORDER BY can use any column of the table, shown or not

options.text: The directory ordered by name, since the SELECT list holds name and title and the database drops an ORDER BY column outside it
options.says: the page's run sorted by cost, a column the SELECT didn't return

options.text: An error from the database, since the SELECT list holds name and title and ORDER BY can only use a column in it
options.says: ORDER BY can use any column of the table; the run sorted by cost while selecting only name

options.text: An error from the database, since the check passes salary as text and H2 reads text after ORDER BY as a column number
options.says: H2 reads a bound parameter in ORDER BY as a column number; a name written into the text is a column name

origin.section: A Bind Parameter Holds a Value, So a Sort Column Comes from an Allow-List

questions.stem: A report server serves `base.resolve(name).normalize()` after checking `startsWith(base)` on the result. Inside base, an operator made `latest` a symbolic link to the backup directory, which is outside base. A request asks for latest/db.dump. What happens?

options.text: The dump is served, since normalize() rewrites the text of the path and doesn't look at links on the disk
options.says: normalize() works on the path's text; the file system follows latest to the backup directory when the file is read

options.text: The dump is served, since startsWith compares the characters of the two paths and the link's name is inside base
options.says: Path.startsWith compares whole name elements, not characters; the dump is served because normalize() never resolves the link

options.text: The request is refused, since normalize() replaces each link in the path with the directory it points to
options.says: normalize() never reads the disk; only toRealPath() follows links

options.text: The request is refused, since resolve() fails for a name whose first element is a symbolic link
options.says: resolve() only appends the name to the base; it doesn't look at the disk

origin.section: A Symlink Inside the Base Points Anywhere; Check the Real Path

questions.stem: A billing import parses invoices with a DocumentBuilderFactory on which the team set the feature `http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities` to false, and nothing else. An invoice declares `<!ENTITY % defs SYSTEM "rates.dtd"> %defs;` in its DOCTYPE. What does the parser do with rates.dtd?

options.text: It reads rates.dtd, since the feature switches off one kind of external entity and %defs; is another kind
options.says: external-general-entities covers general entities only; the page's parameter entity still read its file

options.text: It reads rates.dtd, since the feature switches off entities only in documents read from a URL and not from a file
options.says: the page ties the feature to one kind of entity, not to where the document comes from; with it, order.xml's note came back empty

options.text: It leaves rates.dtd unread, since the feature switches off each kind of external entity and %defs; is one of them
options.says: the feature covers general entities only; the page's parameter entity, also declared with SYSTEM, still read its file

options.text: It leaves rates.dtd unread, since the JDK's factory refuses file access for %defs; unless the team allows it
options.says: the default factory read secret.txt and the parameter entity's file on Java 21; nothing refuses file access unless the code sets it

origin.section: The JDK's XML Parsers Read External Entities Until You Turn Them Off

questions.stem: A message reader sets `in.setObjectInputFilter(info -> known.contains(info.serialClass()) ? Status.ALLOWED : Status.UNDECIDED)`, and the JVM runs without jdk.serialFilter. A message arrives holding a Serializable class that isn't in known and has its own readObject. What happens to that class?

options.text: Its readObject runs, since UNDECIDED leaves the decision to the stream and the stream then allows the class
options.says: a filter answering UNDECIDED let CacheWarmer.readObject run; only REJECTED, as in a pattern ending in !*, refuses

options.text: Its readObject runs, since a stream's filter is asked only about the class of the top-level object
options.says: the filter is asked about each class the stream meets, nested ones too

options.text: It is refused before readObject runs, since a filter rejects every class it does not answer ALLOWED for
options.says: UNDECIDED is not a rejection; the class was read

options.text: It is refused before readObject runs, since UNDECIDED falls back to the JVM-wide filter, which rejects by default
options.says: a filter answering UNDECIDED for everything let CacheWarmer.readObject run, so nothing fell back to a rejecting default

origin.section: Check Classes With a Filter Before readObject Builds Them, Not the Result After

concepts: Input pasted after ORDER BY can read hidden data through the order of the rows, and on H2 a semicolon runs a second statement.
A filter that answers UNDECIDED leaves the class allowed when no JVM-wide filter is set, so an allow-list filter ends by rejecting everything else (!*); jdk.serialFilter sets the JVM-wide filter.
Turning off external general entities leaves parameter entities reading files, and setExpandEntityReferences(false) still opens the file.
